claims.statement: audit_dbless_2026_06_15_test.go locks two specific findings against regression: sanitizeCommitMessage must never split a multi-byte UTF-8 rune when truncating to a max length (TestSanitizeCommitMessageUTF8Boundary, using a 70-character Japanese string whose 210-byte length exceeds a 200-byte cap to force the boundary case), and it must strip C0 control characters and DEL while preserving tab/newline, specifically to prevent terminal-escape-sequence injection into git history and WebSocket delivery (TestSanitizeCommitMessageStripsControl).

instrumentation.json's header states the ledger exists because the same class of mistake happened three times before it was built: a v0.5.1 debug endpoint that recorded an approval's raw answer text verbatim (removed in v0.5.2), a v0.5.x wrapper input trace that persisted every keystroke byte unmasked at world-readable 0644 permissions with no retention limit (caught by a pre-release audit and removed in v0.6.0), and a v0.6.0 debug endpoint left enabled by default until immediately before release.

instrumentation.json's rules require registering observability code in the same commit that adds it, require an active entry to carry a hard UTC-calendar due date rather than being tied to a version number (a version-based scheme was tried first and abandoned because nothing in release.yml or the release manual actually advanced the recorded version, leaving two releases with the same stale marker), require a gate on every entry with always-on gates disallowed especially for anything persisting user-input-derived bytes, and require a removed entry to record removedIn with its files verified actually gone.

instrumentation.json separates a files field (an observability feature's own dedicated file, which disappears entirely on removal) from a sharedFiles field (a shared file like server.go the feature only borrows space in) because collapsing the two into one field forces a choice between registering making removal unverifiable or removal being checkable but unenforced, and two entries (ui-input-trace, hub-input-trace) picked the unenforced option before the split existed and were consequently forgotten during cleanup.

scripts/check-instrumentation.mjs runs six checks: unregistered observability-shaped files/patterns not in the ledger; an active entry's due date having passed; a removed entry whose files were not actually deleted; bidirectional mismatch between web/src/debug/index.ts's actual imports and the ledger's active entries; every ledger-listed Go file carrying the //go:build maidebug build tag as the primary guarantee instrumentation cannot compile into a release build; and every active entry carrying artifactNeedles for the release-artifact-cleanliness check, with a removed entry's removedOn date format also validated when present.

check-claude-md.mjs's header states CLAUDE.md grew from 129 to 269 lines in five weeks (by 2026-08-19) purely from seven dated established-rule sections that each duplicated content with a canonical home elsewhere, and that promoting content into CLAUDE.md is an established practice with no corresponding demotion mechanism, making the file a one-way ratchet without deliberate counter-pressure.

check-claude-md.mjs checks three things (total line count against a budget, whether any single section is too long, and whether a dated established section names its canonical source) and prescribes a fix order when the budget is exceeded: first check whether the rule can be machine-enforced by a script or Go test, second whether it concerns a specific file and can move into that file's own header comment, and third whether it is a yes/no adoption decision belonging as one row in the declined-directions reference ledger; only a rule matching none of the three may keep its full text in CLAUDE.md.

The Validate workflow's go-check job is matrixed across operating systems (name: Go (${{ matrix.os }})) and its jobs block begins with an instrumentation-ledger check job whose comment references the same three near-incident pattern (v0.5.1, v0.5.x, v0.6.0) as instrumentation.json's own header, replacing a 'remove it once the cause is confirmed' comment-only convention with a machine check.
